style: English psych folk funk, 100 BPM: an older, smoky baritone out of South London, gravel at the edges, deep and warm with a Brixton lilt, glottal stops and dropped H's, murmuring the verses in slow conversational talk-singing that never turns into a rapper's flow, a crafty old closing-time storyteller leaning in low like he's letting you in on a secret, then opening up into a warm, gospel-tinged baritone belt on the hook, rounded and held in check, while the regulars at the bar shout the words back. Tin whistle out front over hand drums, congas and a squelchy envelope-filter funk bass with fuzz riding on top of it. Leslie-swirled Hammond organ, a phased wah guitar break. Dubbed-out psych layers: offbeat guitar skanks drenched in spring reverb, delay throws off the echo chamber trailing off line endings. Tucked well behind the band: a low male opera chorus humming and chanting sustained Verdi-crowd notes, French horns, timpani rolling up each build.
exclude: sitar, tabla, drone, Indian, comedy, novelty, parody, kazoo, cartoon, trap, double-time, fast rap, autotune, EDM, country, smooth R&B, rap, hip hop, boom bap, American accent, screaming, dancehall, ragga, toasting, reggaeton, soprano, operatic lead vocal, metal
lyrics:
[Intro: tin whistle carries the tune straight away, congas and squelchy envelope-filter bass under it, Hammond spinning on the Leslie, one long low male hum far in the distance, no drone]

[Verse One: low talk-singing, smoky gravel-voiced storyteller right up on the mic, slow and hushed like a secret, spring-reverb guitar skanking on the offbeat]
They say, ya can't make money from a tree
let's see, each day, make hay, not free, aay
work and get paid though, earning that dough
but where does it go? nobody knows!

means of production means a reduction
standards bleeding, land-lords needing
quantative easing, grandma FREEEEEEEZING!
stimulus checks are next. Get wrecked!

[Aside: muttered under the breath, knowing wink at last orders, groove carries on underneath, echo catches the final word]
rent seeking?... I'm just about eating
sorry, did I interrupt your meeting?
remember kids, the Fed is not your friend!
it prints all the dollars that the government spends

[Build: voice lifting into song, timpani roll growing beneath, French horns and low male chorus sustaining one note behind the band, repeats piling up]
this fiat system is insistent
on debts existence, sooooo
don't be hating on the credit rating
or have resistance to the facts I'm stating

[Hook: warm gospel-tinged baritone belt, rounded and held in check, the bar regulars shouting it back, fuzz riding on the bass riff, Hammond whirling, opera chorus chanting long notes far behind]
Robbery, robbery!
Call the police, it's a robbery!
Debasement! Debasement! It happened in da basement!
Printer is burrrrrrrrring, now now what's occurrrrrrrring?

Robbery, robbery!
Call the police, it's a robbery!
Debasement! Debasement! It happened in da basement!
Printer is burrrrrrrrring, now now what's occurrrrrrrring?

[Verse Two: dub breakdown, only envelope-filter bass and congas, slow smoky talk-singing, repeats spilling off each line]
Stacks and stacks of elastic cash
distracted by a dispraxic flash,
mob, angry at their shitty little job
the right and the left both witness the theft

blaming each other is a sick little cover
institutional, dilutional, the usual
distraction IS the attraction
the intention is tension between the factions

divide and conquer, just look at the hand
It's not ya standard, propaganda, worth a couple grand-ahh
it is, state, level, manipulation
it is the devil, with a radio station

[Build: voice lifting into song, timpani rumbling up, horns swelling, deep male hum behind, splash of spring reverb]
stack up the vaults like a wheelbarrow
risk of default is really rather narrow
Biggie said waaaay back in ninety seven
don't get high off your own supply

[Hook: warm gospel-tinged baritone belt, rounded and held in check, the bar regulars shouting it back, fuzz riding on the bass riff, opera chorus chanting long notes far behind]
Robbery, robbery!
Call the police, it's a robbery!
Debasement! Debasement! It happened in da basement!
Printer is burrrrrrrrring, now now what's occurrrrrrrring?

Robbery, robbery!
Call the police, it's a robbery!
Debasement! Debasement! It happened in da basement!
Printer is burrrrrrrrring, now now what's occurrrrrrrring?

[Instrumental Break: phased wah guitar solo over congas, squelchy fuzzed bass and spinning Hammond, dub echoes]

[Verse Three: hushed conspiratorial talk-singing, tin whistle replying in the gaps]
You know the real star is Pablo Escobar,
who has elastic bands not plastic hands,
stacking up the cash by the grands
standard plans are for the working man

and this right here is a next level scam
ill gotten gains, no need to explain
"bail" and "out", will never mean the same
own the printer and you don't fear winter

[Bridge: rising but restrained, timpani rolling, horns and low male opera chorus stacking up behind the band, echo chamber widening]
crime is asset inflation, passive creation;
of a wealth gap that drives the situation
working people get paid in money, so it's not very funny
when you print more and expect them not to worry

[Last Hook: biggest warm gospel-tinged baritone belt, still rounded and held in check, the whole bar roaring it back, opera chorus and horns behind, every drum and the fuzzed bass going flat out]
hungry people, feed a revolution,
then it's retribution, perhaps some execution
it's time to give, not just to take
but for heaven’s sake, don't just eat cake

[Outro: tin whistle, Hammond and bass, deep male hum fading out, last word echoing away]

[End]
